instructions.name: cancel_round

accounts.name: authority
docs: Permissionless crank caller; plays no role in the outcome (I13).

accounts.name: randomness_account
docs: AUDIT P-1: the round's pinned randomness account. A revealed value
means the outcome is public — the round must settle, never cancel
(otherwise every loser races `fulfill_settle` with a cancel that
voids the winner). A CLOSED account (no longer owned by the oracle
program) cannot reveal anymore, so cancelling stays allowed and an
orphaned pin can always be refunded.
Randomness fallback: may also be the `EntropyChain` singleton
(writable: a cancel releases the chain's pending round). The source
is classified from the account itself (`classify_pinned`), never from
config, so a provider switch cannot turn a revealed account into a
"closed" one.
classified and parsed there.

entry before the prize is claimed, which is exactly why claim must
not consume it).

instructions.name: commit_randomness

via the Switchboard `randomness_commit` CPI (exactly-once).

accounts.name: randomness_account

constrained to the configured oracle program; key equality against
the pin, the authority binding and the unrevealed precondition are
checked in the handler. The oracle program writes the commit below.
in the handler against the round's write-once pin.

accounts.name: queue
docs: The queue pinned in `config.oracle_queue`. Switchboard itself
re-verifies the oracle's queue membership inside the CPI; pinning

queue is verified in the handler.

accounts.name: authority
docs: Permissionless crank caller (I13); plays no role in the outcome.

instructions.name: crank_auto_deposit
docs: Permissionless: enters a funded escrow into an open round, paying
the stake (to the vault), the entry rent and the crank tip (to the
caller) all out of the escrow. The minted entry's `player` is the
escrow PDA.

accounts.name: entry
docs: Same index-unforgeability as `deposit`: the seed is derived from
`round.entry_count` itself, and `init` refuses an existing account,
so index collisions (a human deposit landing mid-flight) fail
cleanly for the caller to retry with fresh indices.

accounts.name: escrow
docs: Bound by its own `owner` field (see module docs): the seed check
alone would accept any PDA of the form ["escrow", x] — this pins x
to the account's self-declared owner, so the escrow presented is
exactly the escrow that will be debited.

accounts.name: crank
docs: The permissionless crank. Pays the entry rent during `init` and is
reimbursed `entry_rent + tip` from the escrow below (R2); with any
tip above ~5_000 lamports the net `+tip − tx_fee` is positive, so
there is no configuration in which a stranger's entry costs the
keeper money. The owner signing here bypasses the window gate.

instructions.name: create_randomness
docs: Permissionless: births the round's Switchboard randomness account
via CPI — the round PDA signs as the account authority (the
deployed `randomness_init` demands the authority's signature).

accounts.name: randomness
docs: The fresh randomness account keypair — signs the transaction, is
written (created) by the oracle program through the CPI below.
to establish inside the CPI.

accounts.name: queue
docs: handler so a crank cannot aim creation at a foreign queue.

accounts.name: payer
docs: Permissionless crank caller; pays the account's creation rent (I13).

accounts.name: lut_signer
docs: program creates it inside the CPI; a fresh account's owner is the
System program, so no owner constraint is possible here). The oracle
program validates it inside the CPI.

instructions.name: deposit
docs: The hot path: escrow native SOL, mint one entry and its ticket range.

accounts.name: entry
docs: A wrong `entry_index` is structurally unforgeable: the seed is
derived from `round.entry_count` itself (ADR-1), and `init` refuses
an existing account, so index collisions fail cleanly for the client
to retry.

accounts.name: escrow
docs: The player profile (Phase 11.6, decision D1): created on the
first-ever bet, reused by every later one. `init_if_needed` is safe
for the same reason as in `init_or_deposit_escrow`: the seed
contains the SIGNER's key, so a different signer derives a
different PDA and cross-owner reinitialisation is structurally
impossible.

accounts.name: mega_pot
docs: Fee sink for the one-time profile charge.

instructions.name: drain_mega_pot_v1_preflight
docs: Admin, one-shot preflight: pays the pre-v2 Mega-Pot out to the
treasury so the migration's `accrued_lamports == 0` guard is
satisfied honestly (under v1 odds the pot can never reach 0 by
itself). Refuses once `economics_version >= 2` or any round is in
flight.

instructions.name: fulfill_settle
docs: Permissionless crank: resolves the winning ticket and moves the cuts.

accounts.name: randomness_account
docs: The exact account pinned at request time: a Switchboard randomness
account, or the `EntropyChain` singleton (writable: settle clears its
`value_round`). Key equality with the pin, the source classification
(`classify_pinned`), authority binding, reveal state and freshness
are all checked in the handler.

accounts.name: authority
docs: Permissionless crank caller (I13); receives the keeper tip, which is
paid out of the 1% admin cut — never a fourth slice.

instructions.name: init_or_deposit_escrow

auto-deposit terms; `amount == 0` changes terms only.

accounts.name: mega_pot

instructions.name: initialize

accounts.name: authority

instructions.name: migrate_economics_v2
docs: Admin, one-way: retunes the economics to the v2 partial-loss model
(ADR-11). Refuses while the Mega-Pot holds lamports or any round is
in flight; after the latch, economics are immutable again.

accounts.name: mega_pot
docs: Read-only: the guard refuses to retune odds while the pot still
holds lamports contributed under them (see guard 2).

accounts.name: rent
docs: Reserved by the cutover checklist for post-migration verification;
the latch itself moves no lamports.

instructions.name: migrate_economics_v3
docs: Admin, one-way: v2 → v3 settlement (the rake falls on the losers'
money only; `fulfill_settle` then requires the winning entry).

instructions.name: open_round
docs: Permissionless: opens round `next_round_id` once no round is `Open`.

accounts.name: payer
docs: Permissionless crank caller; plays no role in the outcome (I13).

accounts.name: previous_round
docs: The active round, when any round has ever been opened. Deliberately
the LAST field: anchor assigns accounts sequentially, so an
`Option<Account>` is only omissible at the tail — clients simply stop
the account list here for the very first round. It cannot carry a
seed constraint (the account legitimately does not exist yet), so it
is bound to `config.active_round_id` in the handler — a program-owned
`Account<Round>` cannot be forged off-PDA, and the round-id field
check pins it to the exact round.

instructions.name: refund_entry
docs: Permissionless: refunds one entry of a cancelled round in full.

accounts.name: entry
docs: The entry being refunded, pinned by seeds to
`(round.round_id, entry_index)` — an entry from another round or
index cannot be presented. `close = player` returns the entry's rent
to the player at instruction exit.

types.name: AccountOpened
docs: A player's `PlayerEscrow` profile was created and the one-time
`account_open_fee_lamports` seeded the Mega-Pot. Charged on top of
rent (recorded separately here) and exactly once per wallet across
both creation paths.

types.name: AutoDeposited
docs: A permissionless crank entered an escrow into a round: one entry minted
with `player = escrow`, the stake moved to the round vault, and the
entry rent + tip reimbursed to the crank out of the escrow.

types.name: ConfigUpdated
docs: AUDIT P-3: every `update_config` emits the effective values of the
levers that matter to players, so indexers and players can see changes.

types.name: Deposited
docs: A deposit minted one entry and its ticket range. `extended` is set when
the anti-snipe timer moved, so the UI can show the clock jumping rather
than appearing to freeze.

types.name: EconomicsMigrated
docs: ADR-11: the one-way economics cutover ran. Carries every after value
(the immutable fee bps are restated for indexer convenience) and both
version numbers; `economics_version` can never move again.

fields.name: commit
docs: `sha256` of the next seed to be revealed.

fields.name: remaining
docs: Seeds left in the current chain.

fields.name: pending_round
docs: The round awaiting a reveal, or `ENTROPY_NONE`.

fields.name: target_slot
docs: The slot whose hash the pending round will use (the first produced
slot at or after it).

fields.name: request_slot
docs: When the pending round was requested.

fields.name: value
docs: The last revealed value; meaningful only while `value_round` is set.

fields.name: value_round
docs: The round `value` belongs to, until it settles; or `ENTROPY_NONE`.

fields.name: value_slot
docs: The slot whose hash produced `value`.

fields.name: revealed_count
docs: Lifetime reveals, for indexers.

types.name: EntropyChainSet
docs: Randomness fallback: the admin set (or rotated) the entropy chain.

types.name: EntropyRevealed
docs: Randomness fallback: a round's entropy was revealed. Carries every
input, so anyone can recompute `value` and check `sha256(seed)` against
the previous commit.

types.name: EntryRefundPaid
docs: A settled round paid one entry its pro-rata slice of `refund_pool` and
(on a trigger) `mega_field_pool` at `close_entry`. `close_entry` is
permissionless and pays `entry.player` — for auto-deposit players that
is the escrow PDA, so the refund lands where `auto_reinvest` can roll
it into the next round; for direct depositors it is the wallet.

fields.name: amount
docs: The entry's stake, for context.

fields.name: refund
docs: Pro-rata share of `refund_pool`.

fields.name: mega_field
docs: Pro-rata share of `mega_field_pool` (0 unless the round triggered).

types.name: EntryRefunded
docs: A cancelled round refunded one entry in full (ADR-7: fees are taken at
settlement only, so refunds are exact).

types.name: EscrowDepleted
docs: An escrow's budget ran dry (or its balance can no longer buy a round);
fired once so the UI and the keeper registry can demote it without
polling. The account survives — the owner can re-fund or withdraw.

types.name: EscrowFunded
docs: An escrow was funded (or re-funded) and its terms set. The keeper's
event-sourced registry keys off this; a missed log is healed by the
next GPA reconciliation.

fields.name: total_lamports
docs: The escrow's post-call on-chain balance (rent floor included).

types.name: EscrowWithdrawn
docs: The owner withdrew spendable escrow lamports to their wallet. Not
pause-gated and carries no config dependency — fund exits keep maximum
liveness.

fields.name: remaining
docs: The escrow's post-withdrawal on-chain balance (rent floor included).

types.name: FeesSwept
docs: The treasury authority swept accrued fees out of the treasury vault.

types.name: GlobalConfig
docs: Program-wide configuration, created once by `initialize`.
Immutable after creation (ADR-10): `fee_bps_admin`, `fee_bps_mega`,
`winner_bps`, `mega_award_bps`, `mega_trigger_modulus`. An admin who can
retune jackpot odds mid-cycle can rug the progressive pot, so this must
be structurally impossible, not merely unauthorized. Everything else
stays admin-mutable; admin transfer is two-step via `pending_admin`.

fields.name: pending_admin
docs: Two-step handoff staging slot; `None` when no transfer is pending.

fields.name: treasury_authority
docs: Fee-sweep destination authority; separate from `admin` for ops hygiene.

fields.name: oracle_program_id
docs: Pinned oracle program id; the randomness account's owner must match.

fields.name: oracle_queue
docs: Pinned Switchboard On-Demand queue; `commit_randomness` only ever
commits against this queue, so a crank cannot steer the round at a
different queue. Admin-mutable (queue migration is operational, not
economic — unlike `oracle_program_id`, which is immutable).

fields.name: fee_bps_admin
docs: Admin cut, bps — **immutable**.

fields.name: fee_bps_mega
docs: Mega-Pot cut, bps — **immutable**.

fields.name: winner_bps
docs: Winner share, bps — **immutable**; the three must sum to 10_000 (I14).

fields.name: mega_award_bps
docs: Mega-Pot award on trigger, bps — **immutable**.

fields.name: mega_trigger_modulus
docs: 1-in-N trigger odds — **immutable**; must be ≥ 1.

fields.name: max_entries_per_round
docs: `0` = unlimited entries.

fields.name: max_round_duration_secs
docs: Hard ceiling on anti-snipe extension.

fields.name: claim_deadline_secs
docs: After this, an unclaimed prize sweeps to the Mega-Pot.

fields.name: anti_snipe_min_deposit_lamports
docs: Only deposits ≥ this extend the anti-snipe timer.

fields.name: keeper_tip_lamports
docs: Paid out of the 1% admin cut — never a fourth slice.

fields.name: randomness_reveal_deadline_slots
docs: Must stay < 512 (`SlotHashes` retention window).

fields.name: next_round_id
docs: Monotonic; ids are never reused.

fields.name: paused
docs: Blocks `deposit` and `open_round` only — never fund-exit paths.

fields.name: auto_deposit_window_secs
docs: Permissionless `crank_auto_deposit` is legal only while
`now <= round.start_ts + this`. Outside it, only the escrow owner
may trigger their own deposit (anti-selection; design §4.2).

fields.name: auto_deposit_tip_lamports
docs: Paid to whoever cranks an auto-deposit, out of the ESCROW — capped
by `MAX_AUTO_DEPOSIT_TIP_LAMPORTS`, never admin-raisable past it.

fields.name: auto_deposit_enabled
docs: Feature kill switch. `false` on the deployed config (its reserved
bytes are zero), so the program upgrade changes no behaviour.

fields.name: refund_bps
docs: Refund share of a settled pot, bps — **immutable** after
`migrate_economics_v2`. The fourth slice: returned to every entry
pro-rata, the winner's included (I14, I18).

fields.name: mega_field_bps
docs: Mega-Pot share paid pro-rata to the field on a trigger, bps —
**immutable**. The winner's share is `mega_award_bps`.

fields.name: mega_payout_cap_bps
docs: Ceiling on a Mega-Pot payout, in bps **of the round's own pot**.
`0` = uncapped (the pre-Phase-11 behaviour). This is the sole
defence against farming the trigger in low-volume rounds, and I21
pins it: a round can never pay out more than it could have been
charged in rake over `mega_trigger_modulus` rounds. `u32`, not
`u16` — the canonical 80_000 exceeds `u16::MAX`.

fields.name: account_open_fee_lamports
docs: One-time fee when a `PlayerEscrow` is first created; seeds the
Mega-Pot. Admin-mutable under `MAX_ACCOUNT_OPEN_FEE_LAMPORTS` —
onboarding cost, not an economic lever (ADR-10 unaffected).

fields.name: economics_version
docs: `0`/`1` = the launch 98/1/1 economics; `2` = four-way partial-loss.
One-way latch, set by `migrate_economics_v2` (ADR-11); read by the
UI to know which rules a round played under.

fields.name: reserved
docs: Forward-compat padding: a field can be added later without migration.
Phase 10 took 17 bytes (8+8+1) for the auto-deposit fields, Phase 11
another 17 (2+2+4+8+1) for the partial-loss economics — both sit
**immediately before `reserved`** so every pre-existing field keeps
its byte offset and the total size stays 340 (zero migration).

types.name: InitializeArgs
docs: Operational parameters. The immutable economics are deliberately absent
(see module docs); everything here stays admin-mutable via
`update_config` (Phase 3B).

fields.name: treasury_authority
docs: Fee-sweep destination authority; separate from `admin` for ops hygiene.

fields.name: oracle_program_id
docs: Pinned oracle program id; `fulfill_settle` will require the
randomness account's owner to match it.

fields.name: oracle_queue
docs: Pinned Switchboard On-Demand queue; commits only ever run against it.

fields.name: max_entries_per_round
docs: `0` = unlimited entries.

fields.name: max_round_duration_secs
docs: Hard ceiling on anti-snipe extension.

fields.name: claim_deadline_secs
docs: After this, an unclaimed prize sweeps to the Mega-Pot.

fields.name: min_deposit_lamports
docs: Suggested 10_000_000 (0.01 SOL): an 8× margin over `PlayerEntry` rent.

fields.name: anti_snipe_min_deposit_lamports
docs: Only deposits ≥ this extend the anti-snipe timer.

fields.name: keeper_tip_lamports
docs: Paid out of the 1% admin cut — never a fourth slice. Default 0.

fields.name: randomness_reveal_deadline_slots
docs: Must stay < 512 (`SlotHashes` retention window).

fields.name: auto_deposit_window_secs
docs: Permissionless `crank_auto_deposit` window (Phase 10). Pass `0`
and `false` to birth the program with the feature off — the
devnet upgrade path reads exactly that from the former reserved
bytes.

fields.name: auto_deposit_tip_lamports
docs: Capped by `MAX_AUTO_DEPOSIT_TIP_LAMPORTS` below.

fields.name: account_open_fee_lamports
docs: One-time PlayerEscrow creation fee, seeds the Mega-Pot (Phase 11,
decision D1: universal — the escrow is the player profile). The one
new economics-adjacent field that is an onboarding cost, not an
odds lever, so it takes the same shape as the tip: an arg under a
compile-time ceiling, admin-mutable later via `update_config`.

types.name: MegaPotContribution
docs: A settled round's 1% cut landed in the progressive pot.

types.name: MegaPotDrainedPreflight
docs: ADR-11 preflight: the pre-v2 Mega-Pot was drained to the treasury so the
migration's `accrued_lamports == 0` guard is satisfied by real
bookkeeping. Booked as a pot payout (`lifetime_awarded`), not a trigger;
the path refuses once `economics_version >= 2`.

types.name: MegaPotTriggered
docs: The 1-in-N event (N = `mega_trigger_modulus`, 625 under Phase 11
economics): the pot fired and its payable split was snapshotted into
the round's vault (ADR-8) — `awarded` for the winner via
`claim_winnings`, `field_pool` pro-rata to every entry via
`close_entry`. Emitted even on a zero balance, so the trigger
statistics stay honest (§8 item 12).

types.name: MegaPotVault
docs: The progressive jackpot, at ["mega_pot"]; singleton.

fields.name: accrued_lamports
docs: The **authoritative spendable balance** (I3). Never compute the
awardable amount from `vault.lamports()` — that includes the
rent-exempt minimum and a 90% award could push the account below
exemption.

fields.name: reserved
docs: Forward-compat padding.

types.name: MigrateEconomicsV2Args
docs: The v2 economics, written once by the latch. Every field is immutable
afterwards; `fee_bps_admin`/`fee_bps_mega` are NOT args (they stay at
their launch values — moving them was never part of the pivot).

types.name: OracleProvider
docs: Which randomness source NEW rounds use. Borsh variant indices pin the
on-chain encoding: `0 = Switchboard`, `1 = Orao` (never implemented),
`2 = Entropy` (the operator hash chain, `EntropyChain`).
Admin-mutable since the randomness-fallback change: the provider is
read when a round requests randomness — after lock, before any value
exists under either source — and a pinned round keeps its source until
it settles or cancels. Settle/cancel/close classify the PINNED account,
never this field, so a flip can never re-route an in-flight round.

types.name: OracleProviderChanged
docs: Randomness fallback: the provider for NEW rounds changed.

fields.name: provider
docs: `0 = Switchboard`, `1 = Orao`, `2 = Entropy`.

types.name: PauseToggled
docs: AUDIT P-3: pause / unpause is public.

types.name: PlayerEntry
docs: One deposit, minted at
`["entry", round_id.to_le_bytes(), entry_index.to_le_bytes()]`.
Keyed by **index, not player** — the player pubkey is a field, and
payouts, refunds and reclaimed rent always route to `entry.player`.
Index keying is what enables the client's O(log n) binary search on
`ticket_start` (ADR-2).
The immutable half-open range `[ticket_start, ticket_end)` partitions
`[0, round.total_lamports)` with every other entry of the round (I9):
`ticket_end` is stored rather than derived so the range check is auditable
at a glance, and `amount > 0` is enforced at deposit — an empty range
would break the partition.
For client indexing: `round_id` sits at byte offset 8 (after the
discriminator) and `player` at offset 20, giving the `memcmp` filters for
`getProgramAccounts`.

fields.name: round_id
docs: Checked against `round.round_id` on every use.

fields.name: player
docs: Sole destination for payout, refund and reclaimed rent.

fields.name: amount
docs: The deposited amount; `> 0` by construction (I8).

fields.name: ticket_start
docs: Inclusive range lower bound — the round's total before this deposit.

fields.name: ticket_end
docs: Exclusive range upper bound.

fields.name: reserved
docs: Forward-compat padding.

types.name: PlayerEscrow
docs: One player's auto-deposit terms and lifetime accounting, at
`["escrow", owner.key().as_ref()]`.
`next_eligible_round_id` is the double-entry guard: `0` at open, set to
`round_id + 1` after each auto-deposit, and **never reset by re-funding**
— re-funding must not re-open a round the escrow already played. Round
ids are monotonic and never reused, so `round_id >= next_eligible` is
simultaneously the same-round and the replay guard (I17).

fields.name: owner
docs: Also the seed. Sole withdrawal authority.

fields.name: per_round_lamports
docs: The stake per round. Re-validated against
`config.min_deposit_lamports` at **every** auto-deposit — the admin
may have raised the floor since the terms were set.

fields.name: max_rounds
docs: Ceiling on `rounds_remaining`; bounds the commitment under
`auto_reinvest`.

fields.name: rounds_remaining
docs: The budget. `0` ⇒ dormant (re-fund or withdraw; no auto-closure).

fields.name: next_eligible_round_id
docs: Double-entry guard (I17): `round_id + 1` after each auto-deposit.

fields.name: rounds_funded
docs: Lifetime count of auto-deposited rounds.

fields.name: lifetime_deposited
docs: Lifetime lamports funded in by the owner.

fields.name: lifetime_staked
docs: Lifetime lamports staked into pots.

fields.name: auto_reinvest
docs: Winnings, refunds and rent rebates that land in the escrow buy more
rounds (capped at `max_rounds`); with the flag off, inbound money
just accumulates until withdrawn.

fields.name: bump
docs: Canonical bump, stored at init.

fields.name: reserved
docs: Forward-compat padding.

types.name: PrizeClaimed
docs: The winning entry proved membership and was paid.

types.name: RandomnessCommitted
docs: The round PDA itself committed its pinned randomness account through the
Switchboard On-Demand `randomness_commit` CPI — the commit half of ADR-4.
The account's authority is the round PDA, so only this program can ever
commit, and exactly once. `seed_slot` is read back from the account after
the CPI; `fulfill_settle` re-checks its freshness against `lock_slot`.

types.name: RandomnessRequested
docs: The round pinned its randomness account (ADR-4). There is exactly one
such event per non-cancelled-at-lock round; re-pinning is impossible.

fields.name: signature
docs: The oracle gateway's secp256k1 signature over the committed slothash.

fields.name: value
docs: The revealed value — belt-checked against what the CPI wrote.

types.name: Round
docs: One round of the pari-mutuel pool at ["round", round_id.to_le_bytes()].
`total_lamports` doubles as the exclusive upper bound of the ticket space;
the half-open ranges of the round's entries partition `[0, total)` (I9).

fields.name: end_ts
docs: Mutated by anti-snipe extension only.

fields.name: lock_slot
docs: Security ordering lives here (slots), not in `lock_ts` (timestamps).

fields.name: settle_ts
docs: Start of the claim deadline clock.

fields.name: total_lamports
docs: Also the exclusive upper bound of the ticket space.

fields.name: entry_count
docs: Next `entry_index`.

fields.name: entries_closed
docs: Cleanup progress; the round closes only at `entries_closed == entry_count`.

fields.name: single_depositor
docs: `true` until a *different* player deposits — O(1) sole-depositor detection.

fields.name: randomness_account
docs: Pinned once by `request_randomness` (ADR-4, no re-rolls).

fields.name: randomness_commit_slot
docs: Timeout clock for `cancel_round`.

fields.name: randomness_seed_slot
docs: Recorded at settle for public audit.

fields.name: winning_ticket
docs: `< total_lamports` whenever `Settled` (I10).

fields.name: winner
docs: Zero until claimed (ADR-2): settle records a ticket, claiming proves
membership. Indexers read `winning_ticket`, not `winner`.

fields.name: mega_awarded
docs: Mega-Pot award snapshotted at settle time (ADR-8).

fields.name: vault_owed
docs: ADR-6: lamports this round's vault still owes someone. The single
balance invariant — `vault.lamports() == rent_minimum + vault_owed`
holds after every instruction in every state.

fields.name: refund_pool
docs: Settle-time obligation to the field: the pot's refund slice, taken
as the exact residual of `total_lamports` so I18 holds to the
lamport. Drawn down pro-rata by `close_entry`.

fields.name: refunds_paid
docs: Running total actually paid out of `refund_pool` (I20).

fields.name: mega_field_pool
docs: Mega-Pot field share snapshotted into the vault at settle (ADR-8);
`0` when the trigger did not fire.

fields.name: mega_field_paid
docs: Running total actually paid out of `mega_field_pool` (I20).

fields.name: rent_payer
docs: Who funded this round's two rent-exemptions at `open_round`. The
deterministic reclaim destination at `close_round`, so the crank
recovers its own capital instead of donating it to the admin.
`Pubkey::default()` on rounds opened before Phase 12 — those fall
back to `config.admin`, which is exactly the old behaviour.
Carved out of the former forward-compat padding in place (Phase 11
had already taken the 32 bytes before it for the refund/mega-field
pools): same offset, same width — `Pubkey` is exactly `[u8; 32]`,
so every pre-existing field keeps its byte offset, the total stays
302, and the rounds already live on devnet decode the all-zero tail
as the legacy sentinel.

types.name: RoundCancelled
docs: A round entered the terminal refund state.
`reason`: `0` = zero deposits (**historical** — pre-Phase-12 `lock_round`
cancelled empty rounds; since the window roll, no instruction produces
it, but devnet logs and indexers still carry it), `1` = sole depositor,
`2` = oracle timeout.

types.name: RoundDustSwept
docs: At `close_round`, the two pro-rata pools' rounding dust (at most one
lamport per entry each, I22) swept to the Mega-Pot — the single
residual sink. Dust never reaches the treasury.

types.name: RoundLocked
docs: The deposit window closed.

types.name: RoundOpened
docs: A new round began accepting deposits.

types.name: RoundSettled
docs: The economic core: outcome and split of a settled round. Carries
`winning_ticket`, `total_lamports` **and** the raw `randomness_value` so
any third party can independently recompute the outcome — public
verifiability is a product feature here, not just hygiene.
**Phase 11 semantics change — indexers must be told:** `winner_payout`
now means *the 9% winner slice* (`floor(total × winner_bps/10_000)`),
not the v1 98% residual; the residual lives in `refund_pool`, paid
pro-rata to every entry by `close_entry`.

fields.name: winner_payout
docs: The winner's slice (9% of the pot under v2 economics).

fields.name: refund_pool
docs: The field's slice, drawn down pro-rata by `close_entry`.

fields.name: mega_field_pool
docs: The Mega-Pot field share snapshotted into the vault (ADR-8); `0`
when the trigger did not fire.

types.name: RoundState
docs: Round lifecycle. One-way (invariant I12); `Settled` and `Cancelled` are
absorbing terminal states. Note the roadmap's five states — the extra
`AwaitingRandomness` between `Locked` and `Settled` is what makes ADR-4's
pin/freshness/timeout guarantees expressible at all.

types.name: RoundVault
docs: Escrow for one round's deposits, at ["round_vault", round_id_le].
Kept separate from `Round` (ADR-8): co-locating data and lamports would
make every balance assertion subtract a rent minimum that changes with
the data length. Holds lamports only.

fields.name: reserved
docs: Forward-compat padding.

types.name: RoundWindowRolled
docs: An empty `Open` round's deposit window rolled forward in place (Phase
12): same `Round` account, same `RoundVault`, same parked rent — no
teardown, no reopen, no state change. The idle-burn fix's on-chain
footprint: one 5 000-lamport transaction instead of a
4 128 360-lamport close/open pair. `reason` distinguishes who rolled —
see the `ROLL_REASON_*` constants.

fields.name: start_ts
docs: The new window start — `now` at roll time (R2: both timestamps
move, so `crank_auto_deposit`'s window and the anti-snipe absolute
cap stay meaningful).

fields.name: end_ts
docs: The new window end — `now + config.round_duration_secs`.

fields.name: reason
docs: `0` = rolled by `lock_round` (keeper or community crank);
`1` = revived by `deposit` (the first bettor's own transaction).

types.name: TreasuryVault
docs: Fee sink, at ["treasury"]; singleton drained by `admin_sweep_fees`.

fields.name: accrued_lamports
docs: Sweepable balance (I2: `lamports == rent_min + accrued_lamports`).

fields.name: reserved
docs: Forward-compat padding.

types.name: UnclaimedPrizeSwept
docs: An unclaimed prize lapsed into the Mega-Pot — value stays in the game
rather than becoming protocol revenue.

types.name: UpdateConfigArgs
docs: Operational updates. `None` leaves a field untouched.

fields.name: max_round_duration_secs
docs: Hard ceiling on anti-snipe extension.

fields.name: claim_deadline_secs
docs: After this, an unclaimed prize sweeps to the Mega-Pot.

fields.name: anti_snipe_min_deposit_lamports
docs: Only deposits ≥ this extend the anti-snipe timer.

fields.name: keeper_tip_lamports
docs: Paid out of the 1% admin cut — never a fourth slice.

fields.name: randomness_reveal_deadline_slots
docs: Must stay < 512 (`SlotHashes` retention window).

fields.name: oracle_queue
docs: Queue migration is operational, not economic — unlike the oracle
program id, which stays structurally absent here.

fields.name: auto_deposit_window_secs
docs: Phase 10 auto-deposit surface (operational, ADR-10-compatible):
the permissionless-caller window, the crank tip, and the feature
kill switch. The tip can only ever move *underneath*
`MAX_AUTO_DEPOSIT_TIP_LAMPORTS`.

fields.name: account_open_fee_lamports
docs: Phase 11: the one-time PlayerEscrow creation fee. The sole
economics-adjacent field allowed here — an onboarding cost, not a
jackpot-odds lever (R7/ADR-10), movable only underneath
`MAX_ACCOUNT_OPEN_FEE_LAMPORTS`.

fields.name: oracle_provider
docs: Randomness fallback: the source NEW rounds request from. Rounds
already pinned keep theirs (settle/cancel classify the pinned
account), so switching is safe at any time. Operational, not
economic: it changes no odds, fees or payouts.
